intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the sakura season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls selling dango and taiyaki. Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play beneath the blossoms.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a stunning world of interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike are captivated by the light, sound, and motion exhibits that respond to touch and movement. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience that blends technology with Japanese aesthetics.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. Walk through narrow lanes packed with vendors and learn about Japanese culinary culture. A self-guided tour is budget-friendly and endlessly exciting for curious eaters of all ages.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys while adults enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra cultural flair.

experiences.name: Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in beautiful kimonos and participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a tea master in a traditional tatami room. Learn the art of matcha preparation, the philosophy of wabi-sabi, and the etiquette of Japanese hospitality. Many studios near Gion offer family-friendly sessions with English guidance.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly airport limousine bus or local train to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront area). Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings. Enjoy the coastal scenery and spot any early cherry blossom trees in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local shopping street (shotengai) or convenience stores (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) to stock up on snacks and essentials. Grab a simple dinner nearby and rest to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or onigiri from a convenience store at the airport (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Local ramen shop or gyudon chain restaurant like Yoshinoya or Sukiya near the hotel (¥600–¥900)

day_by_day.notes: Use IC cards (Suica or Pasmo) for all public transport – load ¥3,000–¥5,000 at the airport. Convenience stores are your best friends for budget meals in Japan. April 15 is peak cherry blossom season so expect crowds at popular spots.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to the nearest local park or riverside path for a morning hanami (cherry blossom viewing) walk. Bring a convenience store breakfast and enjoy it under the blooming sakura trees. Look for free public parks with sakura trees – a quintessential Japanese spring experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Shinto shrine or Buddhist temple. Most shrines are free to enter and offer a deep cultural experience. Walk the grounds, observe local worshippers, and try drawing an omikuji (fortune slip) for ¥100–¥200. Explore the surrounding neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local izakaya (Japanese pub) for an affordable dinner with small shared dishes. Many izakayas offer all-you-can-drink deals and hearty food at budget prices. Try yakitori (grilled chicken skewers) and edamame.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and canned coffee from a convenience store (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Soba noodle restaurant near the shrine – cold or hot zaru soba (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Local izakaya – yakitori, edamame, miso soup (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a picnic mat (available at 100-yen stores like Daiso) for hanami sitting. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Most shrine grounds are free but inner halls may charge ¥300–¥500.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local history or folk museum in the area. Many regional museums charge ¥300–¥500 admission and offer fascinating exhibits on Japanese history, traditional crafts, and local culture. Look for free museum days which often occur on specific dates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a traditional Japanese market or covered shopping arcade. Browse handmade crafts, local produce, and street food stalls. Try taiyaki (fish-shaped cake filled with red bean) or takoyaki (octopus balls) as a snack (¥300–¥500).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event – check local community boards for traditional music performances, tea ceremony demonstrations, or ikebana (flower arranging) workshops. Many cultural centers offer free public events in spring.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or toast and coffee from a Doutor or Komeda's Coffee café (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Street food at the market – takoyaki, yakisoba, or grilled corn (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal restaurant – rice, miso soup, grilled fish, and pickles (¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Check local tourism websites or hotel front desk for free cultural events. The 100-yen store Daiso is great for affordable souvenirs and travel essentials. Bring cash as many small vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a family-friendly attraction such as a public aquarium, science museum, or children's park. Many cities have affordable family admission rates. Look for municipal facilities which are significantly cheaper than private theme parks (¥500–¥1,500 per adult).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for an interactive shopping experience – great fun for families and kids. Then visit a local game center (arcade) where many games cost ¥100 per play. Try the claw machines and purikura (photo booth) for memorable family photos.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from a local supermarket (visit after 7pm for discounted bento boxes and sushi marked down 20–50%). Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hotel or nearby park.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast – sandwiches, yogurt, and juice (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Family restaurant (famiresu) like Gusto or Saizeriya – kids meals available, affordable portions (¥600–¥1,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Discounted supermarket bento boxes and sushi packs (¥500–¥800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many Japanese aquariums and museums offer family discounts. Children under 6 are often free. Supermarket discount hours are typically 7–9pm – look for yellow discount stickers on packaged foods.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19 (Day Trip to Nearby City)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early local train to a nearby city or town for a day trip. Research the cheapest rail pass or IC card fare. Arrive and visit the main castle, park, or cultural landmark. Japanese castles typically charge ¥500–¥700 admission and offer panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the city's historic district or preserved merchant town (machiya). Walk through narrow lanes lined with traditional wooden buildings, small craft shops, and tea houses. Visit a free garden or riverside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by early evening. Stop at a local depachika (department store basement food hall) to pick up affordable prepared foods, fresh sushi, and pastries for a budget dinner picnic.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before catching the train (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Local specialty dish of the day-trip city – try the regional ramen, udon, or soba (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Depachika food hall picks – sushi, salads, and Japanese sweets (¥700–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check train schedules the night before and load enough on your IC card. Avoid bullet trains (shinkansen) to keep costs low – local and rapid trains are much cheaper. Carry a water bottle as vending machine drinks add up.

day_by_day.morning: Seek out a famous local cherry blossom spot – riverside paths, castle moats, or hilltop parks are ideal. Arrive early (before 9am) to avoid crowds and enjoy peaceful sakura photography. Many of these spots are completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join or observe a local hanami picnic atmosphere. Buy picnic supplies from a convenience store or supermarket. Lay out a mat under the cherry trees and enjoy the quintessential Japanese spring experience with onigiri, sandwiches, and canned drinks.
day_by_day.evening: If the area has yozakura (night cherry blossom viewing with lanterns), visit after dark for a magical atmosphere. Many parks illuminate sakura trees at night for free. End the evening with a warm bowl of ramen.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Hanami picnic – onigiri, sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from convenience store or supermarket (¥600–¥900 per person)
meals.dinner: Ramen restaurant – tonkotsu, shoyu, or miso ramen (¥700–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: April 20 is likely still within peak sakura season. Bring a blanket or picnic mat. Hanami spots can be crowded on weekends – arrive early. Alcohol is allowed in most public parks during hanami season.

day_by_day.morning: Participate in a budget-friendly traditional craft workshop – options include origami, calligraphy (shodo), or pottery. Community centers and cultural halls often offer these for ¥500–¥1,500. This is a wonderful hands-on cultural activity for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a large Buddhist temple complex. Walk through the main hall, explore sub-temples, and observe monks going about their daily routines. Many temple gardens charge a small fee (¥300–¥500) but the atmosphere is priceless.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local shotengai (covered shopping arcade) in the evening. Browse affordable souvenir shops, try street food snacks, and soak in the lively local atmosphere. Look for kakigori (shaved ice) or dango (rice dumplings) stalls.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) – morning set with toast, egg, and coffee (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Udon restaurant – kake udon with toppings (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) – budget option with plates starting at ¥100–¥150 each (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Look for community center (kominkan) workshops for the cheapest craft experiences. Temple etiquette: bow slightly at the gate, don't photograph worshippers, and be quiet in prayer areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take advantage of the hotel's beachfront location. Enjoy a morning walk along the beach, collect shells, and watch local fishermen at work. Visit a nearby fishing port if available – morning fish markets are fascinating and often free to observe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore coastal temples or shrines, which are common in Japan's beachfront areas. Many feature dramatic torii gates near the water. Visit a local seafood market and try fresh seafood snacks directly from vendors at very affordable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the beach or a coastal viewpoint. Have dinner at a local seafood restaurant near the port – fresh fish is often cheaper and more abundant in coastal towns. Try a seafood donburi (rice bowl) or grilled whole fish.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store near the beach (¥300–¥600)
meals.lunch: Fish market snacks – grilled scallops, fresh shrimp, or seafood skewers (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Coastal seafood restaurant – seafood donburi or grilled fish set meal (¥900–¥1,400)

day_by_day.notes: Coastal areas in Japan often have unique regional seafood specialties. Ask locals or hotel staff for their favorite affordable seafood spots. Bring sunscreen as April sun near the coast can be strong.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a large public park for a final cherry blossom appreciation walk (late blooms may still be visible). Take family photos among the petals. Explore any free botanical gardens or riverside trails in the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicated souvenir shopping day. Visit 100-yen stores for affordable gifts (Japanese snacks, chopsticks, keychains). Head to a local department store or specialty shop for higher-quality omiyage (regional souvenirs). Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner as a trip celebration – try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant with a set course menu, or visit a teppanyaki grill. Many offer lunch-priced dinner sets for great value.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or kissaten morning set (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Curry rice restaurant – Japanese-style curry with rice and pickles (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner – shabu-shabu all-you-can-eat or teppanyaki set (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Best budget souvenirs: regional Kit Kat flavors, matcha sweets, tenugui (hand towels), and small ceramics. Avoid airport souvenir shops as they are significantly more expensive. Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid breakage.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take a final peaceful walk along the beachfront or to a nearby viewpoint. Enjoy a slow breakfast and soak in the last moments of Japan. Pack carefully and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Use any remaining yen to buy last-minute airport snacks or duty-free items. IC card balances can be refunded at airport machines (small handling fee applies). Spend remaining coins on vending machine drinks or small snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 10 incredible days in Japan!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or final convenience store meal in Japan (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Airport food court – soba, udon, or bento box (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Refund IC card balance at green Suica machines at the airport. Declare any food items when passing customs at your home country. Keep receipts for tax-free purchases as you may need to show them at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the sakura season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls selling dango and taiyaki. Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play beneath the blossoms.

Children and adults alike are captivated by the light, sound, and motion exhibits that respond to touch and movement. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience that blends technology with Japanese aesthetics.

experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. Walk through narrow lanes packed with vendors and learn about Japanese culinary culture. A self-guided tour is budget-friendly and endlessly exciting for curious eaters of all ages.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys while adults enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra cultural flair.

experiences.name: Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in beautiful kimonos and participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a tea master in a traditional tatami room. Learn the art of matcha preparation, the philosophy of wabi-sabi, and the etiquette of Japanese hospitality. Many studios near Gion offer family-friendly sessions with English guidance.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Journey time approximately 60–90 minutes depending on location.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation stroll along the beachfront promenade near the hotel to get your bearings and recover from the flight. Pick up a local SIM card or pocket Wi-Fi from a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart).
day_by_day.evening: Light first dinner close to the hotel — visit a nearby casual ramen or izakaya restaurant to ease into Japanese cuisine. Try classic tonkotsu ramen or yakitori skewers. Early night to beat jet lag.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or onigiri from a convenience store or airport food hall after landing
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood izakaya or ramen shop near the resort — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize rest on Day 1. Set alarms to stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to help adjust to the time zone. Pick up an IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for seamless public transport throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: After a proper night's rest, enjoy breakfast at the resort or a nearby café. Head to the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — arrive by 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats while exploring one of Japan's most iconic food destinations.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tsukiji, make your way to the TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum. Spend 2–3 hours immersed in the mesmerizing interactive digital art installations — a perfect family activity that blends technology and creativity. Book tickets in advance online to avoid queues.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Odaiba or Shibuya area depending on proximity. Try a family-friendly shabu-shabu (hot pot) restaurant where everyone cooks their own food at the table — fun and interactive for all ages.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) — try a traditional morning set (toast, egg, coffee) for ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Snack your way through Tsukiji Outer Market — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person for tastings
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu restaurant — mid-range set menus around ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be pre-booked online — check the official site for timed entry slots. Tsukiji is best visited in the morning when produce and energy are freshest. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — approximately 2 hours 15 minutes. Depart by 8:00–9:00 AM to maximize your day. Check luggage into a coin locker at Kyoto Station upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. April is prime cherry blossom season — enjoy the iconic weeping cherry tree in full bloom. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy sakura mochi and drinks from nearby stalls, and soak in the magical atmosphere with your family.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gion district at dusk — stroll the lantern-lit streets of Hanamikoji and keep an eye out for geiko and maiko. Dinner at a traditional Kyoto kaiseki-style restaurant for a curated multi-course meal showcasing seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Grab onigiri and coffee from a Tokyo convenience store before boarding the Shinkansen
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Maruyama Park — purchase bento boxes and sakura-themed snacks from stalls in the park (¥800–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Kyoto kaiseki or obanzai (Kyoto home-style cuisine) restaurant in Gion — mid-range set menus ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance via the JR Pass or at the station. Maruyama Park is free to enter. Evening in Gion is magical during cherry blossom season — the park may also be illuminated at night (yozakura). Check local event listings for evening light-up schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience in Kyoto. Dress your family in beautiful kimonos and participate in an authentic tea ceremony led by a tea master. Many venues in the Higashiyama district offer this experience with English guidance — allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Still dressed in kimonos (if the rental allows), walk through the picturesque Higashiyama district — visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched on the hillside with stunning spring views, and browse the charming Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with souvenir shops and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return kimonos and head to Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous 'Kitchen of Kyoto' — for an early evening snack walk. Dinner at a cozy tofu cuisine restaurant, a Kyoto specialty.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or guesthouse breakfast, or a nearby café with Japanese morning set
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a teahouse near Kiyomizudera — try yudofu (tofu hot pot) or soba noodles (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Kyoto-style tofu kaiseki restaurant near Nishiki Market — ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the kimono and tea ceremony experience in advance — popular slots fill up quickly, especially on weekends in cherry blossom season. Many kimono rental shops allow you to keep the kimono for the full day for great photo opportunities. Kiyomizudera entrance fee is approximately ¥500 per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine with thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the mountain. Arrive before 8:00 AM to enjoy it without the crowds. Walk as far up the trail as your family is comfortable — even the first 30 minutes offers spectacular photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the Arashiyama district. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — best experienced in the early afternoon light. Afterward, visit the Arashiyama Monkey Park (Iwatayama) — a short uphill hike leads to a hilltop where Japanese macaques roam freely with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Great for kids!
day_by_day.evening: Relax along the Oi River in Arashiyama — enjoy the weeping cherry trees that line the riverbanks. Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Arashiyama with views of the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast or hotel breakfast before heading to Fushimi Inari
meals.lunch: Casual noodle restaurant near Arashiyama — try soba or udon (¥900–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Arashiyama — seasonal kaiseki or grilled fish set menus ¥2,500–¥4,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours — early morning is strongly recommended. Arashiyama Monkey Park has an entrance fee of approximately ¥600 per adult and ¥300 per child. Wear sturdy shoes for the monkey park hike. The bamboo grove is a short walk from the main Arashiyama station.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara — approximately 45 minutes from Kyoto by train. Visit Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming sika deer greet visitors. Purchase deer crackers (shika senbei) and let the kids hand-feed the deer. Walk to the magnificent Todai-ji Temple housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns lining the forested pathways. Stroll through Naramachi, the preserved merchant district, and browse local craft shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Farewell dinner in Kyoto at a popular yakitori restaurant — skewered grilled chicken and vegetables paired with cold Asahi beer (or soft drinks for the kids) in a lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or bakery near Kyoto Station before departing
meals.lunch: Nara-style kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf-wrapped sushi) bento or a casual restaurant in Naramachi (¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Yakitori restaurant in Kyoto — set menus ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Todai-ji entrance fee is approximately ¥600 per adult. The deer in Nara Park can be pushy when they smell the crackers — keep bags zipped and supervise young children closely. Nara is easily done as a half-day or full-day trip from Kyoto. Return by 17:00 to enjoy a relaxed evening.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto to Osaka by train (approximately 15 minutes on the Shinkansen or 30–40 minutes on the local Hankyu/JR line). Check in to your Osaka accommodation or store luggage. Begin with a visit to Osaka Castle — explore the castle tower museum and enjoy the surrounding park, which is also dotted with cherry blossoms in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori — Osaka's vibrant entertainment and food district. Cross the Ebisu Bridge for the iconic Glico Man sign photo, then explore the neon-lit streets. Visit the Dotonbori food stalls and try Osaka's famous street foods.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Dotonbori and Shinsaibashi — enjoy the electric atmosphere, browse shops, and have dinner at one of Osaka's legendary kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Kyoto hotel breakfast or a quick café stop before departing
meals.lunch: Dotonbori street food feast — try takoyaki (octopus balls), okonomiyaki (savory pancake), and taiyaki (fish-shaped pastry) — budget ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person
meals.dinner: Kushikatsu restaurant in Dotonbori — all-you-can-eat options available for ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Osaka Castle entrance fee is approximately ¥600 per adult, children free. The castle park grounds are free. Dotonbori is extremely lively in the evening — perfect for family exploration. Remember the golden rule of kushikatsu: never double-dip the skewers in the communal sauce!

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan — one of the world's largest and most impressive aquariums, featuring whale sharks, manta rays, and thousands of marine species. Ideal for families and easily a 2–3 hour experience. Located in the Tempozan Harbor Village area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the aquarium, ride the giant Tempozan Ferris Wheel for panoramic views of Osaka Bay. Then head to Umeda Sky Building for its famous floating garden observatory — a stunning architectural landmark with sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Umeda/Namba area for dinner. Try a conveyor belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) for a fun and interactive family dining experience — fresh sushi circulates on a belt and you pick what you like.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a morning visit to a local bakery or café
meals.lunch: Casual restaurant in the Tempozan area or a food court near the aquarium — try udon or ramen (¥900–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant in Namba or Umeda — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kaiyukan tickets are approximately ¥2,400 per adult and ¥1,200 per child — book online to save time. The Tempozan Ferris Wheel is approximately ¥900 per person. Umeda Sky Building observatory is approximately ¥1,500 per adult. Consider combining these with an Osaka Amazing Pass if doing multiple attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Hiroshima — approximately 1.5 hours from Osaka by Shinkansen. Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum — a deeply moving and important cultural experience. The A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a powerful symbol of peace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry from Hiroshima to Miyajima Island — famous for the 'floating' Itsukushima Shrine and its iconic red torii gate rising from the sea. Explore the island, encounter friendly deer, and hike or take the ropeway up Mount Misen for sweeping views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Osaka by Shinkansen. Light dinner near your hotel — try Osaka-style okonomiyaki at a local teppanyaki restaurant where the chef cooks the savory pancake on a hot iron griddle right in front of you.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing for Hiroshima
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (a regional specialty layered with noodles) near the Peace Park — ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki okonomiyaki restaurant in Osaka — ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum entrance is approximately ¥200 per adult. The museum content is sobering — use your discretion with very young children. Miyajima ferry is approximately ¥180 each way. The floating torii gate is best seen at high tide — check tide tables in advance. Ropeway to Mt. Misen is approximately ¥1,000 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and do any last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit a local department store basement (depachika) for beautifully packaged Japanese sweets and snacks as gifts. Popular picks: matcha Kit Kats, wagashi (traditional sweets), and regional food specialties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before international departures for check-in and security. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at one of the airport restaurants — many Japanese airports have excellent ramen, sushi, and tempura options.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 wonderful days of cherry blossoms, culture, and family memories across Tokyo, Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a beloved local café — savor a last matcha latte and Japanese pastry
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant — try a classic tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set or sushi platter as a farewell meal (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Leave extra time for airport transfer — Osaka Kansai International Airport (KIX) is approximately 75 minutes from the city center by Haruka Express. If departing from Tokyo Narita or Haneda, plan accordingly. Return any rented pocket Wi-Fi devices at the airport. Keep some yen for airport meals and any last purchases as many small shops are cash-only.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the sakura season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls selling dango and taiyaki. Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play beneath the blossoms.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a stunning world of interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike are captivated by the light, sound, and motion exhibits that respond to touch and movement. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience that blends technology with Japanese aesthetics.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. Walk through narrow lanes packed with vendors and learn about Japanese culinary culture. A self-guided tour is budget-friendly and endlessly exciting for curious eaters of all ages.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys while adults enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra cultural flair.

experiences.name: Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in beautiful kimonos and participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a tea master in a traditional tatami room. Learn the art of matcha preparation, the philosophy of wabi-sabi, and the etiquette of Japanese hospitality. Many studios near Gion offer family-friendly sessions with English guidance.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort arranged with a meet-and-greet service, chilled towels, and welcome refreshments in the vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront suite. Enjoy a private resort orientation tour, relax on the beachfront terrace, and take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline to decompress after the long-haul flight.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Enjoy a curated kaiseki-inspired tasting menu featuring seasonal spring ingredients, paired with premium sake selections and ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or pre-arrival)
meals.lunch: Light bento box or premium snack box arranged in the transfer vehicle
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — multi-course kaiseki tasting menu with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Avoid heavy scheduling on Day 1 to allow the family to adjust to the time difference. Confirm resort concierge has all upcoming reservations pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — start the day with a guided premium small-group tour of Tokyo's most iconic food market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and artisan street foods. Perfect for awakening the palate and diving into Japanese culinary culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum — immerse the entire family in breathtaking interactive digital art installations. The fluid, boundaryless rooms create a magical and awe-inspiring experience for all ages. Book a private or priority-access slot to avoid queues.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the upscale Ginza district. Visit a renowned sushi omakase restaurant where the chef curates a personalized 12–15 course meal using the finest seasonal fish and ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast featuring Japanese and Western options, freshly squeezed juices, and premium pastries
meals.lunch: Gourmet tastings at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh uni, otoro sushi, tamagoyaki, and seasonal pickles
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi restaurant in Ginza — premium 12-course chef's selection with sake or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Teamlab Borderless tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. Tsukiji tour is best started around 8–9am for the freshest produce — arrange an early departure from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — arrive early to beat the crowds and experience the spiritual atmosphere of Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. A knowledgeable private guide will explain the history, rituals, and cultural significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the traditional craft shops and boutiques along Nakamise-dori shopping street. Visit a high-end lacquerware and ceramics studio for a hands-on family workshop creating personalized Japanese pottery or calligraphy scrolls.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails and dinner at a rooftop sky lounge with panoramic views of Tokyo's glittering skyline. Enjoy contemporary Japanese fusion cuisine with premium wagyu beef courses and signature cocktails inspired by Japanese botanicals.

meals.breakfast: In-room private breakfast service at the resort — Japanese-style set with miso soup, grilled fish, rice, and seasonal pickles
meals.lunch: Traditional soba noodle lunch at a century-old buckwheat soba restaurant near Asakusa
meals.dinner: Rooftop sky lounge restaurant — contemporary Japanese fusion tasting menu with wagyu beef and cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: The pottery or calligraphy workshop is a wonderful family bonding activity. Arrange for finished pieces to be shipped home by the concierge. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Asakusa.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury Shinkansen (bullet train) transfer to Kyoto. Settle into first-class green car seating with bento boxes prepared by the resort. Arrive in Kyoto in approximately 2.5 hours and check in to a luxury ryokan in the Higashiyama district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience — dress the entire family in beautifully fitted kimonos chosen by a professional kimono dresser, then participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a certified tea master in a historic machiya townhouse.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the lantern-lit cobblestone streets of Higashiyama in your kimonos (if rented for the evening) and enjoy a private kaiseki dinner at your ryokan, served in your tatami suite by a dedicated attendant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — Japanese set meal with fresh tofu, pickled vegetables, and green tea
meals.lunch: Premium bento box enjoyed aboard the Shinkansen featuring regional specialties
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki dinner at the Kyoto ryokan — 10-course seasonal tasting menu served by private attendant

day_by_day.notes: The kimono experience typically lasts 2–3 hours including dressing and the ceremony. Confirm ryokan check-in time and arrange luggage forwarding service (takkyubin) from the resort to the ryokan in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — experience hanami under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree at its peak spring bloom. Arrive early with a private guide for a serene, crowd-free experience. A private picnic setup with premium bento boxes, matcha, and sakura wagashi sweets will be arranged under the blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walk through Gion, Kyoto's historic geisha district. Explore hidden alleys, visit a traditional ochaya (teahouse), and learn about the art of the geiko and maiko. Visit Yasaka Shrine draped in cherry blossom petals.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at a renowned Gion kappo restaurant — a rare intimate dining experience at a counter where the chef prepares each dish personally, using the finest Kyoto-sourced ingredients and seasonal cherry blossom-themed presentations.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan morning meal — traditional Japanese breakfast with grilled fish, dashimaki tamago, tofu, miso soup, and pickles
meals.lunch: Private hanami picnic in Maruyama Park — premium bento boxes, sakura mochi, and premium cold-brew green tea
meals.dinner: Exclusive kappo restaurant in Gion — intimate counter dining with chef's seasonal tasting menu and Kyoto sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom peak in mid-April 2027 is expected to align well with this visit. Confirm bloom forecasts closer to the date. The Gion evening walk may offer a rare sighting of a geiko or maiko — ask your guide for the best timing.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park — walk through the ethereal bamboo forest at dawn for a magical, crowd-free experience. Continue to Iwatayama Monkey Park for a family-friendly encounter with Japanese macaques with panoramic views over Arashiyama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private rickshaw (jinrikisha) tour through Arashiyama's scenic riverside paths and historic temples, including Tenryu-ji's stunning Zen garden. Visit a premium matcha plantation in Uji for an exclusive tea tasting and private garden tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto for a private cooking class at a luxury culinary studio — learn to prepare authentic Kyoto cuisine including dashi broth, tofu dishes, and seasonal vegetable preparations. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the ryokan before departure to Arashiyama
meals.lunch: Riverside kaiseki lunch at a premium Arashiyama restaurant overlooking the Oi River and cherry blossom-lined banks
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the private Kyoto cooking class, enjoyed with curated sake and plum wine selections

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Bamboo Grove before 7am for the best experience with minimal crowds. The Monkey Park involves a moderate uphill walk — suitable for most ages but confirm with younger family members. Rickshaw tours should be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Fushimi Inari Taisha — explore the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the sacred mountain. A private guide will lead the family through lesser-known paths, sharing the spiritual history and symbolism of the shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nara by private luxury car. Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Todai-ji Temple housing the Great Buddha, and hand-feed the free-roaming sacred deer in Nara Park. Explore the Isuien Garden for a tranquil and photogenic cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto for a private geisha entertainment dinner (ozashiki) — an extraordinarily rare and exclusive cultural experience where a geiko and maiko perform traditional dances, play instruments, and engage guests in traditional parlor games.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast — seasonal Japanese set with premium Kyoto-style tofu and house-made pickles
meals.lunch: Traditional Nara-style lunch at a heritage restaurant near Todai-ji — featuring persimmon leaf sushi (kakinoha-zushi) and local specialties
meals.dinner: Ozashiki dinner in a private Gion ochaya — multi-course kaiseki with geiko and maiko entertainment

day_by_day.notes: The ozashiki dinner is one of Japan's most exclusive cultural experiences and requires advance booking through a trusted intermediary or concierge — confirm this months ahead. Nara deer are friendly but can be pushy; keep food bags concealed until ready to feed.

day_by_day.morning: Private Zen meditation and mindfulness session at a historic Kyoto temple with a resident monk. Learn the fundamentals of zazen (seated meditation), participate in the monk's morning routine, and experience the profound stillness of a centuries-old Zen garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping excursion on Shijo-dori and in the Nishiki Market area — visit premium Japanese craft boutiques, artisan knife shops, and high-end department stores. Stop at Nishiki Market for gourmet tastings of pickled vegetables, fresh yuba, and seasonal sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Kyoto dinner at one of the city's Michelin-starred restaurants — a celebratory fine-dining experience featuring the pinnacle of Kyoto kaiseki cuisine with exquisite plating, seasonal ingredients, and world-class service.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the early temple meditation session — rice porridge (okayu) and pickles served at the temple
meals.lunch: Gourmet tastings at Nishiki Market followed by a sit-down lunch at a premium tofu cuisine restaurant (yudofu specialty)
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Kyoto — full seasonal tasting menu with premium sake and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Zen meditation session typically begins very early (around 6am). Confirm timing and dress code with the temple. Shopping in Nishiki Market is best in the early afternoon before it gets crowded. Pack carefully for the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer back to Tokyo via Shinkansen. Check in to a five-star luxury hotel in Tokyo (Aman Tokyo, The Peninsula, or Park Hyatt recommended). Freshen up and enjoy the hotel's sky-high amenities including pool, spa, and lounge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive private tour of the Imperial Palace East Gardens and Chidorigafuchi moat — one of Tokyo's most beautiful cherry blossom spots, where boats drift beneath arching blossom canopies. A private guide will provide historical context of the Imperial grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a world-renowned Tokyo sky bar followed by an extraordinary dinner at a celebrated Tokyo restaurant — choose between world-class teppanyaki with A5 wagyu, or an exclusive sushi counter experience for a grand finale dining event.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast at the Kyoto ryokan before departure — final traditional Japanese set meal
meals.lunch: Premium bento box on the Shinkansen or light lunch at the Tokyo hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Tokyo landmark restaurant — A5 wagyu teppanyaki or exclusive sushi omakase with champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: Chidorigafuchi moat boat rentals are extremely popular during cherry blossom season — arrange a private or priority booking through the concierge. Confirm Tokyo hotel check-in time and arrange luggage forwarding from Kyoto if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Tokyo — enjoy a premium hotel breakfast and last-minute luxury shopping in Omotesando (Tokyo's Champs-Élysées), visiting flagship stores of Japanese designers and artisan boutiques. Pick up curated Japanese gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private farewell experience — visit the Nezu Museum with its exquisite collection of Asian art and a tranquil traditional garden, or opt for a relaxing spa treatment at the hotel's luxury wellness center to prepare for the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport with ample time for departure. Enjoy access to the premium airport lounge with full dining, spa, and relaxation facilities before boarding. Depart Japan with extraordinary memories of culture, cherry blossoms, and family moments.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast buffet — premium spread including Japanese, French, and international options with freshly brewed specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Final Tokyo lunch at a celebrated ramen or tonkatsu restaurant in Omotesando for a casual yet delicious farewell meal
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge dining or early dinner at a celebrated restaurant near the hotel before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5 hours before international departure for check-in and security. The concierge should arrange all luggage handling, airport transfer, and lounge access. Consider purchasing a curated omiyage (souvenir) gift set from Isetan or Takashimaya as a final keepsake.
